svg.aria-label: Reconstruction of the validation layer, showing warnings that are surfaced while the run continues alongside errors that stop the run. All examples are invented.
svg.text: Warnings a person should see, errors the system refuses
A reconstruction, not a screenshot. Every example below is invented for this illustration.
Surfaced for review. None of these are the system’s call to make.

g.text: Week 7 pacing was resolved from the preceding week’s plan
No explicit entry was imported for week 7; the inference is stated rather than hidden.
Gr 4 writing has no room assigned in period 2
A schedule can be produced without it. Whether that is acceptable is a judgement.
Two adults are free for one group in period 5
Possibly deliberate, possibly a waste of a person. Flagged, not resolved.
A protected planning block was moved to fit coverage
Legal and schedulable, and exactly the kind of change someone should know about.

svg.text: States the system will not produce, however plausible the output would look.

g.text: R. Castellanos is assigned to Rm 7 and Rm 15 in period 3
One person, two rooms, one period. There is no correct way to ship this.
The imported plan references a group that no longer exists
Resolving it to the nearest match would guess at something only a person knows.
Period 6 leaves Gr 3 reading without a required adult
A gap that reads as a complete schedule is worse than a refusal to produce one.
Two groups are scheduled into Rm 12 in period 1
Caught before anyone walks a group of children to a room that is already full.

svg.text: The split is the design. A warning is information a person needs in order to decide; an error is a state the system will not emit at all,
because the failure mode here is not a crash. It is a schedule that looks entirely reasonable and is quietly wrong.
This is the logic the test suite exists for: 5,936 tests collected, 5,930 passing, 6 skipped, none failing, on 19 October 2026.
